This is an [R Markdown](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com) Notebook. When you execute code within the notebook, the results appear beneath the code. 

Try executing this chunk by clicking the *Run* button within the chunk or by placing your cursor inside it and pressing *Cmd+Shift+Enter*. 


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(janitor)
library(stringr)
```

```{r}
md_county_pop <- read_csv("md_county_pop.csv")

md_crime <- read_csv("md_crime2023-2024.csv") #crime specifically from MD  

NIBR <- read_csv("nibrs_2024.csv") #National Incident based report for 2024; collects detailed crime data from law enforcement agencies across the United States

```

--What does it contain and what time period does it cover?
  Each row in md_county_pop represents the population size of every Maryland county. And each row in md_crime is an incident report of crime from 2023-2024. 

--Which columns will be most important for your analysis?
 ** From md_crime: county_name, incident date, offense_name, offense_category_name, location_name, crime_against
 **  From md_county_pop: population

--What's missing that you might need or want?
 ** I need to join my md_county_pop dataframe with the md_crime by county so I have a single dataframe with the crime and population statistics; i can get median income from acs 2023. 
 
```{r}
crime_select <- md_crime |>
select(county_name, incident_date, offense_name, offense_category_name, location_name, crime_against)
```


```{r}
md_crime |>
group_by(offense_name) |>
  summarise(
    count = n()
  ) |>
  
arrange(desc(count)) |>
  head()
```

Question: Which offense is most common in each county — and which county–offense combos are highest overall?
```{r}
 most_common_offense <- crime_select |>
   group_by(county_name, offense_name) |>
  summarise(
    count= n()
  ) |>
  
  arrange(desc(count))
```



```{r}
pg_crime <- most_common_offense |>
  filter(county_name ==  "PRINCE GEORGE'S") |>
  group_by(offense_name) |>
  arrange(desc(count)) |>
head()
```


```{r}
baltimore_crime <- most_common_offense |>
  filter(county_name ==  "BALTIMORE") |>
  group_by(offense_name) |>
  arrange(desc(count)) |>
head()
```


```{r}
montgomery_crime <- most_common_offense |>
  filter(county_name ==  "MONTGOMERY") |>
  group_by(offense_name) |>
  arrange(desc(count)) |>
head()

```
 
```{r}
 anne_arundel_crime <- most_common_offense |>
  filter(county_name ==  "ANNE ARUNDEL") |>
  group_by(offense_name) |>
  arrange(desc(count)) |>
head()
```

```{r}
baltimore_city_crime <- most_common_offense |>
  filter(county_name ==  "BALTIMORE CITY") |>
  group_by(offense_name) |>
  arrange(desc(count)) |>
head()

```
